skill.displayName: AI Short Film Finalization — Route C (Flow Free)

version.changelog: v1.0.1: Republished with explicit ClawHub token authentication.

llm.summary: The skill is not clearly malicious, but it under-discloses sensitive logged-in browser automation and local command/file-write behavior behind a narrower film-finalization description.

dimensions.detail: The frontmatter describes post-generation finalization, but the body expands into full RPA shot generation on Google Vids, Flow, and Gemini using the user's already logged-in browser session. Review-package generation is purpose-adjacent; authenticated browser automation materially broadens the capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly use Chrome DevTools Protocol, Playwright, randomized human-like actions, existing Google login state, cookie-carrying downloads, and later executable fix commands. These are disclosed in the body but not narrowly scoped or gated enough for the sensitivity involved.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill includes a Python helper and HTML template, and instructs installing playwright-core in a hard-coded managed Node workspace. Static scan was clean and VirusTotal telemetry was absent, but install and command-execution expectations are not surfaced in the frontmatter.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local ffmpeg extraction and review HTML generation fit the film workflow, but reusing a live Google session and automating third-party web services is high-impact compared with the stated finalization use case. Hard-coded user-specific paths also reduce portability and clarity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence or destructive system behavior was found, but the workflow depends on privileged browser session reuse. The review script also builds output filenames from storyboard titles without sanitization, which can write artifacts outside intended directories if the project input is malicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the agent automate a logged-in Google browser session and run local media-processing commands. Use a dedicated browser profile/account, keep Chrome CDP closed except during the task, review generated execution commands before running them, and only process trusted storyboard files until filename sanitization is added.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Partly supported: the artifact does not clearly advertise shell execution, package installation, local reads/writes, and session-based browser automation in its frontmatter, although those behaviors are visible in the body.
[TP4] expected: Review package generation and extraction of clips, audio, frames, and manifests are coherent with film finalization, so this portion is downgraded; it is not hidden or unrelated.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported: the body expands from finalization into RPA-based generation on Google services, which changes the trust boundary and is not aligned with the frontmatter's narrower 'shots already generated' framing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: the skill instructs connecting to an already logged-in Chrome session over CDP and reusing Google authentication state, which is sensitive and under-scoped for a general finalization skill.
[SDI-2] expected: Package installation and command execution are expected for local media automation, but should be clearer and less tied to hard-coded user-specific runtime paths.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported: the overview and body describe a broader generation pipeline than the frontmatter indicates.
[OH1] unexpected: Supported: review-final-v4.py derives clip, audio, and frame output paths from raw storyboard titles without sanitizing path separators or validating the resolved output location.
